summary: The Comoros issues visas on arrival: the Comoros Mission to the UN gives the fee for a visa obtained on the spot as EUR 60 for stays of up to 45 days, while the UK and French foreign ministries quote about EUR 30, paid on arrival.

primarySources.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Comoros — Permanent Mission to the UN: passport and visa process (visa on the spot for visitors)

fee.notes: Comoros Mission to the UN: EUR 60 for a 45-day visa on arrival (EUR 250 for one year, EUR 500 for ten years), in an undated letter from the mission’s ambassador that has been online since at least 2016. The UK FCDO (page updated December 2025) and France’s foreign ministry quote EUR 30. The Comorian figure is published because the destination’s own mission outranks foreign travel advice.

passportValidity.text: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive in the Comoros.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Comoros travel advice: entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for the Comoros. The UK Foreign Office advises having travel insurance that covers local treatment and unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — the Comoros travel advice (health)

onwardTicket.text: France's foreign ministry says French tourists need a return ticket to obtain the visa on arrival. No Comorian source we could read states a ticket requirement.

source.name: France — Ministère de l’Europe et des Affaires étrangères, Conseils aux voyageurs: Comores, entrée / séjour

proofOfFunds.text: France's foreign ministry says French tourists getting the visa on arrival must show EUR 30 for each day of their stay, together with a return ticket and the address where they will stay. No Comorian source we could read publishes an amount.

source.name: France — Ministère de l’Europe et des Affaires étrangères, Conseils aux voyageurs: Comores, entrée / séjour

payments.text: The Government of Canada says the economy is mostly cash-based, ATMs are not widely available, banking facilities are minimal and most businesses don't accept credit cards. The UK Foreign Office adds that there are very few banks or ATMs on any of the islands, that you should check in advance whether your hotel accepts your card, and that some hotels and restaurants accept euros but give change in Comorian francs.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says crime levels are low but to take precautions against pickpocketing, and that street crime such as robbery is rare. It says protests and unrest can happen, particularly following elections, and advises avoiding crowds and demonstrations. It warns that boats and ferries between the islands can be overloaded, in poor condition and without life jackets.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Comoros travel advice: safety and security

bestTimeToVisit.text: The Government of Canada says monsoons and rarer tropical cyclones usually occur during the hot and humid rainy season, which runs from December to April, when flooding and landslides can make roads impassable. The UK Foreign Office says tropical cyclones can affect the Comoros between January and May.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says people in the Comoros mainly use cash and there are very few banks or ATMs. Credit cards are not always accepted, and card terminals can fail, so always have cash; some hotels and restaurants accept euros but give change in Comorian francs.

The UK Foreign Office warns that boats and ferries between the three islands can be overloaded, in poor condition and without life jackets, and that overloaded vessels have capsized in Comorian waters with significant loss of life.

Mount Karthala, near Moroni on Grande Comore, is an active volcano; the UK Foreign Office notes it last erupted in 2007 and advises checking its most recent reports and monitoring before you plan a visit, and the Government of Canada advises consulting local authorities before hiking on or around it.

The UK Foreign Office says clothing for men and women needs to cover the body loosely from the shoulders to the knees, and that during Ramadan you should not eat, drink, smoke or chew gum in public in the daytime. Drinking alcohol or being drunk on public highways is illegal.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Comoros?
faq.answer: You need one, but you can get it on arrival: the UK Foreign Office says a visa can be bought on arrival at Hahaya airport or other points of entry, and the Comoros Mission to the UN gives the fee for a visa obtained on the spot as EUR 60 for stays of up to 45 days.

faq.question: How much does the Comoros visa on arrival cost?
faq.answer: The Comoros Mission to the UN gives the fee as EUR 60 for a 45-day visa; the UK FCDO and France's foreign ministry quote EUR 30.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than 45 days in the Comoros?
faq.answer: The arrival visa covers stays of up to 45 days, and the Comoros mission to the UN also lists one-year and ten-year visas. No official source we could read says whether a 45-day visa can be extended.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in the Comoros?
faq.answer: Rarely. The Government of Canada says most businesses don't accept credit cards and ATMs are not widely available, and the UK Foreign Office advises checking in advance whether your hotel accepts your card and always having cash available; it says some hotels and restaurants accept euros but give change in Comorian francs.
